headline: Dry and warm through Friday, then tropical-remnant rain and gusty winds spread into both regions Saturday and Saturday night
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Central Kentucky stays sunny and dry through Friday, with highs near 80 today and in the lower to middle 80s Friday. Moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Isaias should reach southern Kentucky Saturday and spread north during the afternoon, followed by widespread rain and gusty winds Saturday night. The exact arrival time and Saturday high remain less certain because the global guidance differs on how quickly the tropical rain shield advances.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; afternoon relative humidity near 20–25% will make fine fuels easier to ignite
days.forecast: Morning clouds around Danville give way to abundant sunshine. A light north wind and very dry air support highs near 80 to the lower 80s, followed by clear skies tonight. Danville and other sheltered rural locations should cool more efficiently than Lexington, with upper 40s possible in the coolest pockets.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; afternoon relative humidity around 22–28% keeps vegetation unusually dry ahead of the weekend rain
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and warm as surface high pressure shifts east. Most locations should reach the lower 80s, with middle 80s possible in warmer spots. Clouds begin increasing Friday night as tropical moisture approaches from the south, but meaningful rain should hold off through the night.

days.label: Saturday
days.precipitation: 40–60% during the afternoon; 90% or greater Saturday night
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts at issuance; independent analysis identifies heavy rain, localized flooding and southeast wind gusts of 25–35 mph as the primary Saturday-night concerns, with a very low but nonzero tornado risk if the system arrives faster
days.forecast: Mostly cloudy, with rain chances reaching southern Kentucky and spreading north during the afternoon. The earlier the rain arrives, the cooler the daytime high will be. Rain becomes widespread Saturday evening and night as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias move north, with a general 0.75–1.50 inches possible through the broader weekend event and localized totals near 3 inches. Gusty southeast winds accompany the heavier rain.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky gets two more dry and warm days before tropical-remnant moisture arrives Saturday. The best chance for widespread rain and the strongest wind gusts is Saturday night. Saturday's precise high and afternoon rain onset remain the main uncertainties.
kentucky.confidence: High through Friday; moderate on Saturday temperatures and rain onset because ECMWF guidance is slower and warmer than the GFS and NWS timing; moderate-high that widespread rain and gusty winds develop Saturday night

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Dense early fog near Clemson gives way to a warm and mainly sunny Thursday. A shallow northeast-flow wedge develops Friday, bringing more clouds and a cooler but unusually uncertain afternoon. Rain associated with the remnants of Hurricane Isaias begins as early as pre-dawn Saturday and becomes widespread and potentially heavy Saturday into Saturday night, accompanied by gusty northeast to east winds.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; locally dense morning fog around Clemson and nearby lakes reduces visibility below one-quarter mile before improving
days.forecast: Fog and low clouds around Clemson lift and dissipate by late morning, leaving a mainly sunny and warm afternoon. Light south to southeast winds accompany highs in the lower to middle 80s. Clouds increase again tonight as low-level northeast flow begins to strengthen.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts; the large temperature range reflects uncertainty in cloud thickness and the strength of the shallow cool-air wedge
days.forecast: Mostly cloudy and cooler under northeast winds around 5–10 mph, with gusts near 20–25 mph late. The NAM, GFS, ECMWF and NWS cluster from the middle 70s to around 80, while HRRR is a warmer outlier near the middle 80s; persistent clouds would favor the cooler half of the range. A slight chance of rain develops toward daybreak Saturday.

days.label: Saturday
days.precipitation: 80–90% during the day; near 100% Saturday night
days.hazard: No official NWS alerts at issuance; independent analysis identifies heavy rain, localized flooding and northeast-to-east wind gusts of 25–35 mph as the primary concerns
days.forecast: Cool, cloudy and increasingly windy with rain developing as early as pre-dawn and becoming widespread during the day. Rain may become heavy Saturday night as a strengthening southeast low-level jet feeds tropical moisture into the Blue Ridge and upper Savannah basin. One to two inches is plausible through Saturday night, with locally higher totals possible near favored upslope terrain; temperatures may struggle through the 60s.

upstate.bottomLine: After today's fog clears, the Upstate has one more warm afternoon. Friday turns cloudier and cooler, although the size of the cooldown is uncertain. Widespread rain, gusty winds and a localized flooding risk arrive Saturday, with the heaviest rain favored Saturday night.
upstate.confidence: High on today's clearing and warmth; moderate-low on Friday's high because HRRR is substantially warmer than the cooler NWS, NAM, GFS and ECMWF cluster; high on widespread Saturday rain but moderate on exact totals and onset timing

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 8:15–8:30 AM EDT. KCEU reported fog with visibility near 0.24 mile, while nearby KLQK was clear, demonstrating the localized character of the morning fog. The NWS point forecasts were generated at 7:05 AM EDT for Danville and 8:31 AM EDT for Clemson.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:36 AM and 6:53 AM EDT. Louisville supports dry warmth through Friday, Saturday-afternoon rain expansion and widespread Saturday-night rain with gusts up to 25–35 mph. Greenville-Spartanburg supports a Friday cool-air wedge and widespread Saturday rain, with excessive rainfall possible Saturday night into Sunday.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either forecast point at the approximately 8:42 AM EDT check. This official alert status is separate from the independent discussion of dense morning fog, Saturday heavy rain, localized flooding and gusty winds.

Model inventories checked at 8:43 AM EDT showed the complete 06Z HRRR through hour 48, complete 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS and GEFS mean through hour 384, and 06Z ECMWF through hour 144. The newer 10Z and 11Z rapid-refresh cycles were incomplete, and no 12Z cycle was substituted for the complete guidance.

College of DuPage radar at 8:35 AM EDT showed both forecast regions precipitation-free. Clean-infrared imagery at 8:31 AM EDT showed the primary tropical cloud shield remaining south of both regions, while official surface observations confirmed localized fog and low cloud near Clemson.

Friday's Upstate guidance differs meaningfully but can be represented without halting publication: HRRR is near 84°F, while NAM is near 75°F, GFS near 80°F, ECMWF near 78°F and the NWS point forecast is 77°F. The 73–82°F forecast range favors the cooler multi-model cluster because the NWS discussion expects a cool-air wedge and notes that thicker clouds could make even its current high too warm; confidence is reduced.

Saturday timing and rainfall totals remain uncertain. The GFS is faster and wetter in Central Kentucky, while ECMWF is slower there; both support a cool, wet Upstate Saturday. The forecast therefore separates lower daytime Kentucky probabilities from 90% or greater Saturday-night probabilities and uses deliberately wide Saturday temperature ranges.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 10:31 AM EDT October 7 was consulted. Kentucky overnight ranges were shifted 1–2°F lower using the recommended KDVK and KLEX corrections. Upstate nighttime ranges were widened in both directions because KCEU has a warm low bias while KLQK has a larger cold low bias. Daytime station corrections remain below the application threshold.

HRRR has the best overall high-temperature mean absolute error among currently scored models, but it was not followed blindly for Friday in the Upstate: it is a warm outlier, and the limited cold-air-damming verification sample favors ECMWF over HRRR, GFS, NAM and RAP. Saturday ranges were widened because 72-hour range coverage is only 48.4%. The low-probability precipitation bin is currently well calibrated, so small dry-day probabilities were retained. This candidate does not modify the repository, forecast archive, website or widget.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted overnight ranges about 1–2°F lower using the recommended KDVK -2°F and KLEX -1°F low-temperature corrections. No daytime station correction was applied because current high-temperature biases remain below the threshold. Saturday's range was widened because 72-hour coverage is only 48.4% and global guidance differs on tropical-rain arrival.

Widened nighttime ranges in both directions rather than applying one correction uniformly because KCEU has a recommended +1°F low correction while KLQK has a recommended -3°F correction. HRRR leads overall high-temperature scoring but was discounted as a Friday warm outlier during a cold-air-damming pattern; the cooler NWS, NAM, GFS and ECMWF cluster received more weight, consistent with the limited regime-specific scores.
